8: #   5 recheck: re-run every confirmed test at the new head (+ ONE step-5-preview call only if untestable blockers were confirmed)

212: touch $G/find.done
213: fi

215: # ---- 2 verify (parallel): failing test per testable claim; script re-runs it
216: verify(){ # verify CANDIDATE_JSON TAG
217:   local c=$1 tag=$2 id; id=$(echo "$c" | python3 -c "import json,sys,re; print(re.sub(r'\W','_',json.load(sys.stdin).get('id','x'))[:30])")
218:   local pf=$G/verify-$tag-$id.md
219:   cat > $pf <<EOF
220: You verify ONE claimed defect in worktree $WT (detached at PR #$PR head $H9; the change is \`git diff origin/${PBASE:-main}...HEAD\`).
221: Claim (JSON): $c
222: 
223: Your job: PROVE or DISPROVE it with a test. Create exactly ONE new test file named test_gate_${LSLUG}_${id}.py in the existing test directory that fits (e.g. api/tests/ for silphcoanalytics, the owning package's tests/ for lake-of-rage). Do not modify ANY other file. The test must exercise the real code path and FAIL at the current head because of the claimed defect (an assertion failure on the wrong behaviour) — not because of import errors, missing fixtures, network or environment. Run it (memory-capped): \`systemd-run --user --scope -q --slice=fleet.slice -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=0 uv run pytest -q <file>\` from the package directory that owns pyproject.toml.
224: If after honest effort the claim is false (the code behaves correctly), delete your test file and answer REJECTED with the evidence. If it truly cannot be shown by a local test, delete the file and answer UNTESTABLE.
225: Final answer: exactly one fenced json block:
226: \`\`\`json
227: {"verdict":"CONFIRMED|REJECTED|UNTESTABLE","test_file":"repo-relative path or null","reason":"one or two sentences of evidence"}
228: \`\`\`
229: EOF
230:   agent rev-gate-$LANE-v$tag-$id $WT $pf 120 >/dev/null 2>&1
231:   alive rev-gate-$LANE-v$tag-$id || repair rev-gate-$LANE-v$tag-$id || { agent rev-gate-$LANE-v$tag-$id $WT $pf 120 >/dev/null 2>&1; alive rev-gate-$LANE-v$tag-$id || { dead "verifier $id"; return; }; }
232:   apply_verdict "$c" "$tag" "$id" "$(extract $R/rev-gate-$LANE-v$tag-$id.out)"
233: }
234: apply_verdict(){ # apply_verdict CLAIM TAG ID VERDICT_JSON — re-run the test; only a real assertion failure confirms
235:   local c=$1 tag=$2 id=$3 v=$4
236:   local verdict tf; verdict=$(echo "$v" | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('verdict','REJECTED'))" 2>/dev/null); tf=$(echo "$v" | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('test_file') or '')" 2>/dev/null)
237:   if [ "$verdict" = CONFIRMED ] && [ -n "$tf" ] && [ -f $WT/$tf ]; then
238:     local o prc
239:     if [ -n "${BATCH_RC:-}" ] && [ "$BATCH_RC" -lt 2 ] && grep -qxF "$tf" <<< "$BATCH_FILES"; then
240:       # batched re-run (verify_batch ran every confirmed file in one pytest call): this file confirms only if one of
241:       # its own tests failed in that run
242:       if grep -q "^FAILED $tf::" <<< "$BATCH_OUT"; then prc=1; else prc=0; fi
243:     else o=$($F/fm_pytest.sh $WT $tf); prc=$?; fi
244:     if [ $prc = 1 ]; then mkdir -p $G/tests; cp $WT/$tf $G/tests/; echo "$c" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); d['test_file']=sys.argv[1]; d['source']=sys.argv[2]; print(json.dumps(d))" "$tf" "$tag" >> $G/confirmed.jsonl; echo "CONFIRMED $id ($tf)" >> $G/log
245:     else echo "DISCARDED $id: verifier said CONFIRMED but re-run rc=$prc" >> $G/log; rm -f $WT/$tf; fi
246:   elif [ "$verdict" = UNTESTABLE ]; then echo "$c" >> $G/untestable.jsonl; echo "UNTESTABLE $id" >> $G/log
247:   else echo "REJECTED $id: $(echo "$v" | cut -c1-200)" >> $G/log; [ -n "$tf" ] && rm -f $WT/$tf; fi
248: }
249: verify_batch(){ # verify_batch CANDIDATES_FILE TAG — one agent writes one test per claim; each is re-run by apply_verdict
250:   local cf=$1 tag=$2; [ -s $cf ] || return 0
251:   if [ "${GATE_VERIFY_BATCH:-1}" != 1 ]; then while read -r c; do [ -n "$c" ] && verify "$c" $tag & done < $cf; wait; return; fi
252:   local pf=$G/verify-$tag-batch.md n=rev-gate-$LANE-v$tag-batch claims
253:   claims=$(python3 $F/lean_gate_claims.py $cf "$LSLUG")
254:   { echo "You verify SEVERAL claimed defects in worktree $WT (detached at PR #$PR head $H9; the change is \`git diff origin/${PBASE:-main}...HEAD\`)."
255:     echo "Claims (one per line):"; echo "$claims"; echo
256:     cat $F/prompts/lean_verify_batch.md; } > $pf
257:   agent $n $WT $pf 250 >/dev/null 2>&1
258:   alive $n || repair $n || { agent $n $WT $pf 250 >/dev/null 2>&1; alive $n || { dead "batch verifier $tag"; return; }; }
259:   local out c id v; out=$(extract $R/$n.out)
260:   # Re-run every test the verifier says is CONFIRMED in ONE pytest invocation (owner 2026-09-26: batch the tests).
261:   BATCH_FILES=$(echo "$out" | python3 -c "import json,sys; [print(x.get('test_file')) for x in json.load(sys.stdin).get('results',[]) if x.get('verdict')=='CONFIRMED' and x.get('test_file')]" 2>/dev/null | while read f; do [ -f "$WT/$f" ] && echo "$f"; done)
262:   BATCH_RC=""; BATCH_OUT=""
263:   if [ -n "$BATCH_FILES" ]; then BATCH_OUT=$($F/fm_pytest.sh $WT $BATCH_FILES); BATCH_RC=$?; echo "batched re-run of $(echo "$BATCH_FILES" | wc -l) test file(s): rc=$BATCH_RC" >> $G/log; fi
264:   while read -r c; do [ -n "$c" ] || continue
265:     id=$(echo "$c" | python3 -c "import json,sys,re; print(re.sub(r'\W','_',json.load(sys.stdin).get('id','x'))[:30])")
266:     v=$(echo "$out" | python3 -c "import json,sys; r=[x for x in json.load(sys.stdin).get('results',[]) if x.get('id')==sys.argv[1]]; print(json.dumps(r[0]) if r else '')" "$id" 2>/dev/null)
267:     [ -n "$v" ] || { dead "batch verifier $tag returned no verdict for $id"; continue; }
268:     apply_verdict "$c" "$tag" "$id" "$v"
269:   done < $cf
270:   BATCH_RC=""; BATCH_OUT=""; BATCH_FILES=""
271: }
272: if [ $RESUME -lt 2 ]; then
273: verify_batch $G/candidates.jsonl f
274: fail_closed
275: st "verify: confirmed=$(wc -l < $G/confirmed.jsonl) untestable=$(wc -l < $G/untestable.jsonl) rejected=$(grep -c '^REJECTED\|^DISCARDED' $G/log)"
276: touch $G/verify.done
277: fi

279: # ---- 3 judge: ONE step-5-preview call
280: jpf=$G/judge1.md
281: cat > $jpf <<EOF
282: You are the final pre-merge judge for PR #$PR ($SLUG) in worktree $WT (detached at $H9). Read-only: do not edit, commit or push. The change is \`git diff origin/${PBASE:-main}...HEAD\`.
283: Evidence so far — confirmed blockers (each has a failing test): $(cat $G/confirmed.jsonl | head -c 6000)
284: Claims a test could not show (rule on each: is it a real merge blocker in the current code?): $(cat $G/untestable.jsonl | head -c 6000)
285: Also do ONE pass of your own for BLOCKERS ONLY (wrong results, data loss, contract breaks, crashes, security, production risk). No style/nits. Each new blocker needs file/line and a concrete repro.
286: Task spec (context): $(echo "$TASK" | head -c 8000)
287: Final answer: exactly one fenced json block:
288: \`\`\`json
289: {"untestable_rulings":[{"id":"...","real":true,"reason":"..."}],"new_blockers":[{"id":"j-1","file":"...","line":1,"claim":"...","repro":"...","testable":true}]}
290: \`\`\`
291: EOF
292: if [ "${GATE_LENSES:-1}" = 1 ] && [ ! -s $G/untestable.jsonl ] && [ "${GATE_JUDGE_ALWAYS:-0}" != 1 ]; then
293:   # nothing for a judge to rule on and a single all-focus reviewer already ran: record an empty verdict, save a stage
294:   printf '```json\n{"untestable_rulings":[],"new_blockers":[]}\n```\n' | tee $R/gate-j1-$LANE.out > $R/rev-gate-j1-$LANE.out
295:   echo 0 > $R/rev-gate-j1-$LANE.exit; st "judge: skipped (1 lens, no untestable claims)"
296: else
297: judge gate-j1-$LANE $WT $jpf
298: fi
299: if [ "${GATE_JUDGE:-cmd}" != grok ] && ! alive rev-gate-j1-$LANE; then judge gate-j1-$LANE $WT $jpf; alive rev-gate-j1-$LANE || { dead "judge1"; fail_closed; }; fi
300: J=$(extract $R/gate-j1-$LANE.out); echo "$J" > $G/judge1.json
301: echo "$J" | python3 -c "
302: import json,sys
303: d=json.load(sys.stdin)
304: for r in d.get('untestable_rulings',[]):
305:     if r.get('real'): print(json.dumps({'id':r.get('id'),'source':'judge-untestable','claim':r.get('reason'),'test_file':None}))
306: " >> $G/confirmed_untestable.jsonl 2>/dev/null
307: echo "$J" | python3 -c "
308: import json,sys
309: for x in json.load(sys.stdin).get('new_blockers',[]): print(json.dumps(x))
310: " > $G/judge_new.jsonl 2>/dev/null
311: verify_batch $G/judge_new.jsonl j
312: fail_closed
313: NU=$( [ -f $G/confirmed_untestable.jsonl ] && wc -l < $G/confirmed_untestable.jsonl || echo 0 ); NC=$(wc -l < $G/confirmed.jsonl)
314: st "judge: new=$(wc -l < $G/judge_new.jsonl) confirmed_total=$NC untestable_real=$NU"
315: 
316: # Merged-tree regression check before any approval: the gate itself only runs the PR's own and gate tests, so a PR
317: # that breaks an untouched existing test (agent-fleet #106 vs the merge-plan suite) could be approved.
318: if [ $NC = 0 ] && [ $NU = 0 ]; then approve; fi
319: 
320: # ---- 4+5 converge: fix rounds continue ONLY while measurable progress is made.
321: #   Each round = one space-bunny fix against the tests failing NOW, then a deterministic re-run of ALL gate tests + the PR's own tests.
322: #   Progress = the failing set strictly shrinks AND no new failures appear. 0 failing -> approve; no progress -> escalate (with metrics).
323: #   GATE_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS (default 4) is only a safety net; the stopping rule is convergence.
324: MAXR=${GATE_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS:-4}
325: ALLT=$( { python3 -c "import json; [print(json.loads(l)['test_file']) for l in open('$G/confirmed.jsonl') if json.loads(l).get('test_file')]" 2>/dev/null; echo "$ptests"; } | grep -v '^$' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
326: runall(){ # runall WORKTREE -> writes failing ids to $2, returns fm rc
327:   local w=$1 out rc; for t in $ALLT; do [ -f $w/$t ] || { [ -f $G/tests/$(basename $t) ] && { mkdir -p $w/$(dirname $t); cp $G/tests/$(basename $t) $w/$t; }; }; done
328:   out=$($F/fm_pytest.sh $w $ALLT); rc=$?; echo "$out" > $2.raw; echo "$out" | awk '/^FAILED /{print $2}' | sort -u > $2; return $rc; }
329: metric(){ python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.dumps(dict(zip(sys.argv[1::2],sys.argv[2::2]))))" "$@" >> $F/gate/metrics.jsonl; }
330: runall $WT $G/fail.0; rc0=$?
331: [ $rc0 -ge 2 ] && { st "NEEDS-ESCALATION gate tests could not run at head ($(grep -E '^(INFRA|SUMMARY)' $G/fail.0.raw | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-160))"; exit 5; }
332: n0=$(wc -l < $G/fail.0); [ $n0 = 0 ] && [ $NU = 0 ] && approve
333: printf "round\thead\tfailing\tfixed\tnew_failures\n0\t%s\t%s\t-\t-\n" $H9 $n0 > $G/rounds.tsv
334: cur=$HEAD0; prev=$G/fail.0; round=0; outcome=""
335: while [ $round -lt $MAXR ]; do
336:   round=$((round+1)); FW=$G/fix$round
337:   git -C $BASE fetch -q origin; wtadd $FW $cur || { st "NEEDS-ESCALATION cannot create fix worktree (base $BASE)"; exit 2; }
338:   for t in $ALLT; do [ -f $FW/$t ] || { [ -f $G/tests/$(basename $t) ] && { mkdir -p $FW/$(dirname $t); cp $G/tests/$(basename $t) $FW/$t; }; }; done
339:   cat > $G/fix$round.md <<EOP
340: Fix PR #$PR ($SLUG) in worktree $FW (detached at ${cur:0:9}; push with \`git push origin HEAD:fb/$LANE\`). Fix round $round.
341: These tests FAIL right now and must pass (each proves a confirmed defect; gate tests named test_gate_*.py are already in the worktree — keep them, never weaken their assertions):
342: $(cat $prev)
343: Defect descriptions: $(cat $G/confirmed.jsonl | head -c 8000)
344: $( [ -f $G/confirmed_untestable.jsonl ] && echo "Also resolve these confirmed (untestable) defects: $(cat $G/confirmed_untestable.jsonl)" )
345: Every other listed test currently passes and must keep passing: $ALLT
346: $( [ -n "$DROPNOTE" ] && echo "$DROPNOTE" )
347: LINT: before committing, run `uv run ruff format` and `uv run ruff check --fix` on every file you added or changed, INCLUDING the gate test files, and keep them free of inline comments; merged gate tests that failed lint turned lake main red. NEVER stop to ask a question and never end without pushing if any listed defect is fixable: fix everything satisfiable, commit, push. If a listed gate test is self-contradictory or asserts behaviour the task never asked for, do NOT weaken or delete it yourself; instead end your final message with one line per such test file: \`UNSATISFIABLE: <path/to/test_file.py> - <one-line reason>\`. An independent judge decides; only judge-rejected tests are removed.
348: Rules: change product code until all of the above pass; run them (memory-capped: systemd-run --user --scope -q --slice=fleet.slice -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=0 uv run pytest -q <files>, from the package dir). Touch nothing unrelated. Commit (never --no-verify; SKIP only a named hook that fails on baseline debt outside your diff) and push. Final message: new head sha and test results.
349: Task spec (context): $(echo "$TASK" | head -c 6000)
350: EOP
351:   agent gatefix$round-$LANE $FW $G/fix$round.md ${GATE_FIX_TURNS:-120} >/dev/null 2>&1
352:   new=$(gh pr view $PR -R $SLUG --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)
353:   DROPNOTE=""; unsat=$(grep -oE 'UNSATISFIABLE: [^ ]+\.py' $R/gatefix$round-$LANE.out 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}' | sort -u)
354:   if [ -n "$unsat" ]; then
355:     { echo "Adjudicate gate tests a fixer called unsatisfiable, for PR #$PR ($SLUG) at ${new:0:9} (read-only; worktree $WT, run git fetch). Task spec: $(echo "$TASK" | head -c 4000)"
356:       echo "Fixer's reasons: $(grep -E 'UNSATISFIABLE:' $R/gatefix$round-$LANE.out | head -c 4000)"
357:       for u in $unsat; do echo "===== $u"; cat $FW/$u 2>/dev/null | head -c 6000; done
358:       echo 'For each file decide DROP only if the test contradicts the task spec or another confirmed test, or asserts behaviour nobody asked for (overfit); otherwise KEEP (a real defect the fixer must still fix). Final answer: exactly one fenced json block: ```json {"drop":["path"],"keep":["path"],"why":{"path":"..."}} ```'; } > $G/adj$round.md
359:     agent gate-adj$round-$LANE $WT $G/adj$round.md 120 >/dev/null 2>&1
360:     drop=$(extract $R/gate-adj$round-$LANE.out | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(' '.join(json.load(sys.stdin).get('drop',[])))" 2>/dev/null)
361:     if [ -n "$drop" ]; then
362:       for d in $drop; do ALLT=$(echo " $ALLT " | sed "s# $d # #g"); grep -v "^$d" $prev > $prev.k; mv $prev.k $prev; done
363:       DROPNOTE="Delete these gate test files (an independent judge rejected them as overfit/contradictory): $drop"
364:       st "round $round: judge dropped overfit gate tests: $drop"
365:     else st "round $round: judge kept all tests the fixer called unsatisfiable"; fi
366:   fi
367:   if [ "$new" = "$cur" ]; then
368:     if [ -n "$DROPNOTE" ] && [ $round -lt $MAXR ]; then st "round $round: no push, but tests were adjudicated; another round"; continue; fi
369:     outcome="no-push"; st "round $round: fixer pushed nothing"; break
370:   fi
371:   RW=$G/re$round; git -C $BASE fetch -q origin; wtadd $RW $new || { st "NEEDS-ESCALATION cannot create recheck worktree (base $BASE)"; exit 2; }
372:   runall $RW $G/fail.$round; rrc=$?
373:   if [ $rrc -ge 2 ]; then outcome="tests-broken"; st "round $round: tests could not run at ${new:0:9}"; break; fi
374:   nf=$(wc -l < $G/fail.$round); fixed=$(comm -23 $prev $G/fail.$round | wc -l); newf=$(comm -13 $prev $G/fail.$round | wc -l); np=$(wc -l < $prev)
375:   printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n" $round ${new:0:9} $nf $fixed $newf >> $G/rounds.tsv
376:   st "round $round @${new:0:9}: failing $np -> $nf (fixed $fixed, new $newf)"
377:   ( flock 200; git -C $BASE worktree remove --force $FW 2>/dev/null ) 200>$F/locks/wt-$REPO.lock; ( flock 200; git -C $BASE worktree remove --force $RW 2>/dev/null ) 200>$F/locks/wt-$REPO.lock
378:   cur=$new
379:   if [ $nf = 0 ]; then
380:     # judge-rejected gate test files still sit in the branch: one more round deletes them before approval
381:     if [ -n "$DROPNOTE" ] && [ $round -lt $MAXR ]; then prev=$G/fail.$round; continue; fi
382:     outcome="converged"; break
383:   fi
384:   # Net progress continues (new failures go into the next round's list); stalled = the failing set did not shrink.
385:   # 19 -> 8 with one new failure was escalated as "stalled" under the old any-new-failure rule.
386:   if [ $nf -ge $np ]; then outcome="stalled"; break; fi
387:   prev=$G/fail.$round
388: done
389: [ -z "$outcome" ] && outcome="cap"
390: if [ "$outcome" = converged ] && [ $NU -gt 0 ]; then
391:   cat > $G/judge2.md <<EOP
392: Recheck for PR #$PR in $SLUG at ${cur:0:9} (read-only; use a fresh \`git fetch\` and inspect \`git diff $HEAD0 $cur\`). These blockers were ruled real earlier and had no test: $(cat $G/confirmed_untestable.jsonl)
393: For each: is it resolved now? Report only unresolved ones.
394: Final answer: exactly one fenced json block: \`\`\`json {"unresolved":[{"id":"...","reason":"..."}]} \`\`\`
395: EOP
396:   judge gate-j2-$LANE $WT $G/judge2.md
397:   if [ "${GATE_JUDGE:-cmd}" != grok ] && ! alive rev-gate-j2-$LANE; then judge gate-j2-$LANE $WT $G/judge2.md; alive rev-gate-j2-$LANE || { dead "judge2"; fail_closed; }; fi
398:   u=$(extract $R/gate-j2-$LANE.out | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin).get('unresolved',[])))" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
399:   [ "$u" = 0 ] || outcome="untestable-unresolved"; st "recheck judge: unresolved=$u"
400: fi
401: metric lane $LANE pr $PR candidates $nc confirmed $NC untestable_real $NU rejected "$(grep -c '^REJECTED\|^DISCARDED' $G/log)" rounds $round outcome $outcome failing_by_round "$(cut -f3 $G/rounds.tsv | tail -n +2 | tr '\n' ',')"
402: [ "$outcome" = converged ] && approve
403: st "NEEDS-ESCALATION ($outcome after $round round(s); failing by round: $(cut -f3 $G/rounds.tsv | tail -n +2 | tr '\n' ' '); see $G/rounds.tsv)"; exit 4

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: source ~/fleet/env.sh
3: # fm_pytest.sh ROOT TEST_PATH... — run tests grouped by nearest pyproject.toml package dir; prints "FAILED <root-relative id>" lines; exit 0 ok, 1 test failures only, 2 infra/collection problem.
4: ROOT=$1; shift; declare -A grp; SEM=$HOME/fleet/fb/sem; mkdir -p $SEM
5: # Result cache (owner 2026-09-26: batch/avoid repeated test runs). Key = git tree of the WHOLE worktree including
6: # uncommitted and untracked files (temp index) + the test list; any code change gives a new key. TTL 24 h.
7: TC=$HOME/fleet/cache/fmtest; mkdir -p $TC; find $TC -maxdepth 1 -type f -mmin +1440 -delete 2>/dev/null
8: _ix=$(mktemp); cp "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --git-path index 2>/dev/null | sed "s#^[^/]#$ROOT/&#")" $_ix 2>/dev/null
9: _tree=$(cd "$ROOT" && GIT_INDEX_FILE=$_ix git add -A . >/dev/null 2>&1 && GIT_INDEX_FILE=$_ix git write-tree 2>/dev/null); rm -f $_ix
10: _key=$(printf '%s %s' "$_tree" "$(printf '%s\n' "$@" | sort | tr '\n' ' ')" | sha256sum | cut -c1-40)
11: if [ -n "$_tree" ] && [ -f $TC/$_key.out ] && [ -f $TC/$_key.rc ]; then cat $TC/$_key.out; echo "CACHE hit $_key" >&2; exit $(cat $TC/$_key.rc); fi
12: exec 3>&1; _cache_out=$(mktemp)
13: trap '_rc=$?; [ -n "$_tree" ] && [ $_rc -lt 2 ] && { cp $_cache_out $TC/$_key.out; echo $_rc > $TC/$_key.rc; }; rm -f $_cache_out' EXIT
14: exec > >(tee $_cache_out >&3)
15: for t in "$@"; do d=$(dirname "$ROOT/$t"); while [ "$d" != "$ROOT" ] && [ ! -f "$d/pyproject.toml" ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; grp[$d]+="${t#${d#$ROOT/}/} "; [ "$d" = "$ROOT" ] && grp[$d]+=""; done
16: worst=0
17: for d in "${!grp[@]}"; do
18:   rel=${d#$ROOT}; rel=${rel#/}
19:   ap=""; grep -q "^\[tool\.uv\.workspace\]" "$d/pyproject.toml" 2>/dev/null && ap="--all-packages"
20:   # memory budget (owner: <=75GB laptop): at most TEST_SLOTS concurrent pytest runs (each capped at 6G)
21:   exec 8>/dev/null; while :; do for i in $(seq 1 ${TEST_SLOTS:-5}); do exec 8>$SEM/test.$i; flock -n 8 && break 2; done; sleep 3; done
22:   out=$(cd "$d" && systemd-run --user --scope -q --slice=fleet.slice -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=0 timeout 1800 uv run $ap pytest -q -rfE -p no:cacheprovider ${grp[$d]} 2>&1); rc=$?
23:   exec 8>&-
24:   echo "$out" | grep -oE "^(FAILED|ERROR) [^ ]+" | awk -v p="${rel:+$rel/}" '{print "FAILED " p $2}'
25:   echo "SUMMARY ${rel:-.}: rc=$rc $(echo "$out" | grep -E "passed|failed|error" | tail -1 | cut -c1-120)"
26:   case $rc in 0) ;; 1) [ $worst -lt 1 ] && worst=1;; *) worst=2; echo "INFRA ${rel:-.}: $(echo "$out" | grep -E "Error|error" | head -2 | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-200)";; esac
27: done
28: exit $worst

1: """Memory-capped pytest execution for the gate's deterministic steps.
2: 
3: Two jobs:
4: 
5: **Cap the memory.** A 36GB pytest runaway is a real failure mode on this machine,
6: so every pytest the gate launches is wrapped in
7: ``systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=0`` when systemd
8: user scopes are available, falling back to ``ulimit -v`` in a subshell. The cap
9: is configurable but the gate never raises it above the configured value.
10: 
11: **Distinguish a test failure from an infra failure.** pytest exit codes are
12: load-bearing here: ``0`` all passed, ``1`` tests failed (a real finding), ``>=2``
13: interrupted / collection error / usage error, which means we learned nothing
14: about the code. The gate treats ``>=2`` as an infra error, never as a blocker.
15: """
16: 
17: from __future__ import annotations
18: 
19: import logging
20: import re
21: import shutil
22: import subprocess
23: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
24: from pathlib import Path
25: from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
26: 
27: if TYPE_CHECKING:
28:     from collections.abc import Sequence
29: 
30: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
31: 
32: # pytest exit codes we act on (see pytest docs, ExitCodes).
33: PYTEST_OK = 0
34: PYTEST_TESTS_FAILED = 1
35: PYTEST_INFRA_ERROR = 2
36: 
37: _MEMORY_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([KMGT]?)B?$", re.IGNORECASE)
38: _FACTOR = {"": 1, "K": 1024, "M": 1024**2, "G": 1024**3, "T": 1024**4}
39: 
40: _TEST_FILE_RE = re.compile(r"(^|/)test_[^/]*\.py$")
41: 
42: _FAILED_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^FAILED\s+(\S+)", re.MULTILINE)
43: _SUMMARY_RE = re.compile(r"^SUMMARY:.*$", re.MULTILINE)
44: 
45: 
46: def memory_to_bytes(value: str) -> int:
47:     """Parse ``6G`` / ``512M`` / ``1073741824`` into bytes."""
48:     match = _MEMORY_RE.match(value.strip())
49:     if not match:
50:         raise ValueError(f"unparseable memory limit: {value!r}")
51:     number, unit = match.groups()
52:     return int(float(number) * _FACTOR[unit.upper()])
53: 
54: 
55: def systemd_run_available() -> bool:
56:     """True when ``systemd-run --user --scope`` can be used on this host."""
57:     if shutil.which("systemd-run") is None:
58:         return False
59:     try:
60:         probe = subprocess.run(
61:             ["systemd-run", "--user", "--scope", "--quiet", "true"],
62:             capture_output=True,
63:             timeout=15,
64:             check=False,
65:         )
66:     except OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError:
67:         return False
68:     return probe.returncode == 0
69: 
70: 
71: def is_test_file(path: str | Path) -> bool:
72:     """True for ``test_*.py`` paths anywhere in a repo (the gate's test selector)."""
73:     return bool(_TEST_FILE_RE.search(Path(path).as_posix()))
74: 
75: 
76: @dataclass(frozen=True)
77: class TestPackage:
78:     """A directory that owns a ``pyproject.toml`` and the tests beneath it.
79: 
80:     Multi-package repos (a root plus an ``api/`` sub-package) need pytest run
81:     from the package directory, not the repo root, so the venv and ``pythonpath``
82:     match. ``dir`` is the package root; ``tests`` are repo-relative paths.
83:     """
84: 
85:     dir: Path
86:     rel_dir: str
87:     tests: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
88: 
89:     @property
90:     def local_tests(self) -> list[str]:
91:         """``tests`` relative to :attr:`dir` — pytest runs with ``cwd=dir``."""
92:         return [to_package_path(self.rel_dir, t) for t in self.tests]
93: 
94:     def command(self, extra: Sequence[str] = ()) -> list[str]:
95:         return [*uv_run_prefix(self.dir), "pytest", "-q", "--no-header", *extra, *self.local_tests]
96: 
97: 
98: def to_package_path(rel_dir: str, repo_path: str) -> str:
99:     """Repo-relative *repo_path* -> path relative to the package at *rel_dir*."""
100:     if rel_dir in ("", "."):
101:         return repo_path
102:     prefix = rel_dir.rstrip("/") + "/"
103:     return repo_path[len(prefix) :] if repo_path.startswith(prefix) else repo_path
104: 
105: 
106: def to_repo_node_id(rel_dir: str, node_id: str) -> str:
107:     """Package-relative pytest node id -> repo-relative (verify/fix/recheck use repo paths)."""
108:     if rel_dir in ("", "."):
109:         return node_id
110:     prefix = rel_dir.rstrip("/") + "/"
111:     return node_id if node_id.startswith(prefix) else prefix + node_id
112: 
113: 
114: def is_uv_workspace_root(package_dir: Path) -> bool:
115:     """True when *package_dir*'s pyproject declares a uv workspace.
116: 
117:     ``uv run`` at a workspace root syncs only the root project, so tests that
118:     import workspace members fail with ModuleNotFoundError in a fresh worktree.
119:     """
120:     try:
121:         text = (package_dir / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
122:     except OSError:
123:         return False
124:     return re.search(r"^\[tool\.uv\.workspace\]", text, re.M) is not None
125: 
126: 
127: def uv_run_prefix(package_dir: Path | None) -> list[str]:
128:     """``uv run`` (+ ``--all-packages`` at a uv workspace root)."""
129:     if package_dir is not None and is_uv_workspace_root(package_dir):
130:         return ["uv", "run", "--all-packages"]
131:     return ["uv", "run"]
132: 
133: 
134: @dataclass(frozen=True)
135: class PytestResult:
136:     """Outcome of one pytest invocation."""
137: 
138:     returncode: int
139:     stdout: str
140:     stderr: str
141: 
142:     @property
143:     def passed(self) -> bool:
144:         return self.returncode == PYTEST_OK
145: 
146:     @property
147:     def tests_failed(self) -> bool:
148:         return self.returncode == PYTEST_TESTS_FAILED
149: 
150:     @property
151:     def infra_error(self) -> bool:
152:         """True when the run told us nothing about the code under test."""
153:         return self.returncode >= PYTEST_INFRA_ERROR
154: 
155:     @property
156:     def failed_ids(self) -> list[str]:
157:         """Node ids of failing tests, parsed from pytest's ``FAILED`` lines."""
158:         return _FAILED_LINE_RE.findall(self.stdout)
159: 
160:     @property
161:     def summary(self) -> str:
162:         matches = _SUMMARY_RE.findall(self.stdout)
163:         if matches:
164:             return matches[-1][:300]
165:         tail = (self.stdout or "").strip().splitlines()[-1:] if self.stdout else []
166:         return tail[0][:300] if tail else ""
167: 
168: 
169: def find_test_packages(
170:     root: Path,
171:     test_files: Sequence[str],
172:     *,
173:     package_dir: str | None = None,
174: ) -> list[TestPackage]:
175:     """Group repo-relative *test_files* by the nearest ancestor with pyproject.toml.
176: 
177:     A file belongs to the deepest directory at or above it that contains a
178:     ``pyproject.toml``; files with no such ancestor fall back to the repo root.
179:     ``package_dir`` forces everything into one package (the single-package case
180:     where the root ``pyproject.toml`` is not the one that owns the tests).
181:     """
182:     by_dir: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
183:     for rel in test_files:
184:         rel_path = Path(rel)
185:         owner = package_dir or _owning_package(root, rel_path)
186:         by_dir.setdefault(owner, []).append(rel_path.as_posix())
187:     return [
188:         TestPackage(dir=root / rel_dir, rel_dir=rel_dir, tests=sorted(tests))
189:         for rel_dir, tests in sorted(by_dir.items())
190:     ]
191: 
192: 
193: def _owning_package(root: Path, rel_path: Path) -> str:
194:     """Relative path of the nearest ancestor directory holding a pyproject.toml."""
195:     parts = rel_path.parent.parts
196:     for i in range(len(parts), -1, -1):
197:         candidate = root / Path(*parts[:i]) if i else root
198:         if (candidate / "pyproject.toml").is_file():
199:             return candidate.relative_to(root).as_posix() if i else "."
200:     return "."
201: 
202: 
203: def build_pytest_command(
204:     test_files: Sequence[str],
205:     *,
206:     memory: str = "6G",
207:     use_systemd: bool | None = None,
208:     package_dir: Path | None = None,
209: ) -> list[str]:
210:     """Build the pytest command, wrapped in a memory cap when possible.
211: 
212:     *test_files* must be relative to *package_dir* (the cwd pytest runs in).
213:     """
214:     inner = [
215:         *uv_run_prefix(package_dir),
216:         "pytest",
217:         "-q",
218:         "--no-header",
219:         *test_files,
220:     ]
221:     if use_systemd is None:
222:         use_systemd = systemd_run_available()
223:     if not use_systemd:
224:         return inner
225:     return [
226:         "systemd-run",
227:         "--user",
228:         "--scope",
229:         "--quiet",
230:         "-p",
231:         f"MemoryMax={memory}",
232:         "-p",
233:         "MemorySwapMax=0",
234:         *inner,
235:     ]
236: 
237: 
238: def run_pytest(
239:     package_dir: Path,
240:     test_files: Sequence[str],
241:     *,
242:     memory: str = "6G",
243:     timeout_s: int = 900,
244:     use_systemd: bool | None = None,
245: ) -> PytestResult:
246:     """Run the given tests from *package_dir* under a memory cap.
247: 
248:     Never raises on a non-zero exit — the caller inspects
249:     :attr:`PytestResult.infra_error` to tell "the code is broken" apart from
250:     "pytest could not run".
251:     """
252:     if not test_files:
253:         return PytestResult(returncode=PYTEST_OK, stdout="", stderr="")
254:     cmd = build_pytest_command(
255:         test_files, memory=memory, use_systemd=use_systemd, package_dir=package_dir
256:     )
257:     logger.debug("gate pytest: %s (cwd=%s)", " ".join(cmd), package_dir)
258:     try:
259:         completed = subprocess.run(
260:             cmd,
261:             capture_output=True,
262:             text=True,
263:             cwd=package_dir,
264:             timeout=timeout_s,
265:             check=False,
266:         )
267:     except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
268:         # A timeout is an infra failure, not evidence the code is broken.
269:         return PytestResult(
270:             returncode=PYTEST_INFRA_ERROR,
271:             stdout="",
272:             stderr=f"pytest timed out after {timeout_s}s",
273:         )
274:     except OSError as exc:
275:         return PytestResult(returncode=PYTEST_INFRA_ERROR, stdout="", stderr=str(exc))
276:     return PytestResult(
277:         returncode=completed.returncode,
278:         stdout=completed.stdout or "",
279:         stderr=completed.stderr or "",
280:     )

1: """Gate pipeline configuration from .agent-fleet.yaml.
2: 
3: The gate is configured per-repo under a ``gate:`` section, with the machine-wide
4: model policy coming from the global ``fleet.yaml`` (``model_policy:``) so every
5: lane on the box shares one approved-model list.
6: """
7: 
8: from __future__ import annotations
9: 
10: import logging
11: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
12: from typing import Any
13: 
14: from agent_fleet.gate.prompts import lane_slug_token
15: 
16: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
17: 
18: # Each lens is one reviewer focus. The four defaults mirror the lanes the
19: # reference gate ran: correctness, contract, production safety, and spec
20: # conformance. A repo can add or replace lenses via ``gate.lenses``.
21: DEFAULT_LENSES: dict[str, str] = {
22:     "correctness": (
23:         "Logic errors, wrong results, broken edge cases, error handling, "
24:         "concurrency/race bugs, regressions of existing behaviour."
25:     ),
26:     "contract": (
27:         "Public API/MCP/schema contract breaks, response shape, params, "
28:         "docs/OpenAPI drift vs behaviour, backwards compatibility, missing "
29:         "tests for promised behaviour."
30:     ),
31:     "prodsafety": (
32:         "Production data safety and ops: data loss, destructive writes, "
33:         "unbounded memory/CPU on the VPS, missing locks/atomicity, unsafe "
34:         "migrations, performance regressions on hot paths, secrets exposure."
35:     ),
36:     "spec": (
37:         "Conformance to the task specification below: required items missing "
38:         "or implemented differently from what was asked."
39:     ),
40: }
41: 
42: DEFAULT_LENS_ORDER: tuple[str, ...] = ("correctness", "contract", "prodsafety", "spec")
43: 
44: _SCALARS: tuple[str, ...] = (
45:     "max_findings",
46:     "max_candidates",
47:     "lens_timeout_s",
48:     "verify_timeout_s",
49:     "judge_timeout_s",
50:     "fix_timeout_s",
51:     "test_timeout_s",
52:     "max_parallel_lenses",
53:     "max_parallel_verifiers",
54:     "max_fix_rounds",
55:     "agent_slots",
56:     "test_slots",
57: )
58: 
59: #: Stages the legacy ``agent_timeout_s`` used to drive, in the order the fixer
60: #: needed it most. The judge is absent because that key never applied to it.
61: _LEGACY_TIMEOUT_KEY = "agent_timeout_s"
62: _LEGACY_TIMEOUT_TARGETS: tuple[str, ...] = ("lens_timeout_s", "verify_timeout_s", "fix_timeout_s")
63: 
64: _STRINGS: tuple[str, ...] = (
65:     "backend",
66:     "judge_backend",
67:     "base_branch",
68:     "test_memory",
69: )
70: 
71: _OPTIONAL_STRINGS: tuple[str, ...] = ("model", "judge_model", "push_branch", "package_dir")
72: 
73: #: Normalised lane slug, used to make gate test file names unique per PR. Empty
74: #: by default so the PR's head ref can supply it at run time.
75: _OPTIONAL_SLUGS: tuple[str, ...] = ("lane_slug",)
76: 
77: _BOOLS: tuple[str, ...] = ("enable_fix", "enable_judge")
78: 
79: #: Pipeline role -> the budget field that governs it. Spelled out rather than
80: #: derived as ``f"{role}_timeout_s"`` because the two vocabularies differ: the
81: #: verifier role is ``verifier`` and its budget is ``verify_timeout_s``.
82: _STAGE_TIMEOUT_FIELDS: dict[str, str] = {
83:     "lens": "lens_timeout_s",
84:     "verifier": "verify_timeout_s",
85:     "verify": "verify_timeout_s",
86:     "judge": "judge_timeout_s",
87:     "fix": "fix_timeout_s",
88: }
89: 
90: 
91: @dataclass(frozen=True)
92: class GateConfig:
93:     """Settings for the ``agent-fleet gate`` PR pipeline."""
94: 
95:     lenses: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_LENS_ORDER
96:     lens_focus: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=lambda: dict(DEFAULT_LENSES))
97:     backend: str = "cmd"
98:     model: str | None = None
99:     judge_backend: str = "cmd"  # owner policy: judge on cmd/space-bunny; grok is opt-in only
100:     judge_model: str | None = None
101:     max_findings: int = 12
102:     max_candidates: int = 12
103:     base_branch: str = "main"
104:     push_branch: str | None = None
105:     enable_fix: bool = True
106:     enable_judge: bool = True
107:     #: Per-stage agent budgets. A single shared number made the fix budget
108:     #: unusable (commit + push + a test suite never fits in a review's budget)
109:     #: while letting a doomed review burn a full stage of wall clock. 40 min for
110:     #: the reviewing stages, 90 for the one that writes and tests code.
111:     lens_timeout_s: int = 2400
112:     verify_timeout_s: int = 2400
113:     judge_timeout_s: int = 2400
114:     fix_timeout_s: int = 5400
115:     test_timeout_s: int = 900
116:     max_parallel_lenses: int = 8
117:     max_parallel_verifiers: int = 6
118:     test_memory: str = "6G"
119:     package_dir: str | None = None
120:     #: Lane slug folded into every verifier-created test file name. Empty means
121:     #: "use the PR's head ref", which is what makes the name unique per PR.
122:     lane_slug: str = ""
123:     # Safety net, not the stopping rule. The fix loop continues while the
124:     # failing set strictly shrinks; ``max_fix_rounds`` only bounds a run that
125:     # keeps making microscopic progress. See docs/GATE.md.
126:     max_fix_rounds: int = 4
127:     agent_slots: int = 24
128:     test_slots: int = 4
129: 
130:     def focus_for(self, lens: str) -> str:
131:         """Reviewer focus text for *lens* (custom or default)."""
132:         return self.lens_focus.get(lens) or DEFAULT_LENSES.get(lens) or lens
133: 
134:     def stage_timeout(self, role: str) -> int:
135:         """The agent budget for *role*, in the pipeline's own vocabulary.
136: 
137:         The mapping is explicit rather than derived from the role name, because
138:         the two vocabularies are not the same: the pipeline's verifier role is
139:         ``verifier`` while its budget is ``verify_timeout_s``. Deriving the
140:         field as ``f"{role}_timeout_s"`` made ``verify_timeout_s`` dead config —
141:         parsed, documented, set in every fleet.yaml, and never applied, so every
142:         verifier silently ran on the reviewing budget instead.
143: 
144:         An unmapped role gets the reviewing budget rather than raising: too
145:         short a stage for a role added later is recoverable, a crash mid-run is
146:         not.
147:         """
148:         return int(getattr(self, _STAGE_TIMEOUT_FIELDS.get(role, "lens_timeout_s")))
149: 
150: 
151: def _apply_legacy_timeout(section: dict[str, Any], kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
152:     """Honour the pre-per-stage ``agent_timeout_s`` without letting it go stale.
153: 
154:     A fleet.yaml written before per-stage budgets sets one number for every
155:     stage that was not the judge. Dropping the key silently would hand those
156:     repos the new defaults and quietly change how long their runs take, so the
157:     value is still applied — to the stages it actually drove — and a warning
158:     names the replacement. An explicit per-stage key always wins, so the
159:     deprecation can be resolved one stage at a time.
160:     """
161:     if _LEGACY_TIMEOUT_KEY not in section:
162:         return
163:     legacy = int(section[_LEGACY_TIMEOUT_KEY])
164:     applied = [key for key in _LEGACY_TIMEOUT_TARGETS if key not in section and legacy > 0]
165:     for key in applied:
166:         kwargs[key] = legacy
167:     logger.warning(
168:         "gate: %s is deprecated; set %s instead (applied to: %s)",
169:         _LEGACY_TIMEOUT_KEY,
170:         " / ".join(_LEGACY_TIMEOUT_TARGETS),
171:         ", ".join(applied) or "nothing (per-stage keys already set)",
172:     )
173: 
174: 
175: def load_gate_config(raw: dict[str, Any] | None) -> GateConfig | None:
176:     """Load the ``gate:`` section; return ``None`` when the gate is disabled.
177: 
178:     ``gate: false`` disables it explicitly, matching the ``code_review: false``
179:     convention. Any other absent/malformed section yields the defaults, so a CLI
180:     ``gate`` run works in a repo with no config at all.
181:     """
182:     section = (raw or {}).get("gate")
183:     if section is False:
184:         return None
185:     defaults = GateConfig()
186:     if not section or not isinstance(section, dict):
187:         return defaults
188: 
189:     focus = dict(defaults.lens_focus)
190:     lenses = defaults.lenses
191:     lenses_raw = section.get("lenses")
192:     if isinstance(lenses_raw, dict) and lenses_raw:
193:         # Mapping form: custom lens name -> focus text replaces the defaults.
194:         focus = {str(k): str(v) for k, v in lenses_raw.items()}
195:         lenses = tuple(focus)
196:     elif isinstance(lenses_raw, list) and lenses_raw:
197:         lenses = tuple(str(name) for name in lenses_raw)
198:     extra_focus = section.get("lens_focus")
199:     if isinstance(extra_focus, dict):
200:         focus.update({str(k): str(v) for k, v in extra_focus.items()})
201: 
202:     kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
203:         "lenses": lenses,
204:         "lens_focus": focus,
205:         "enable_fix": bool(section.get("enable_fix", defaults.enable_fix)),
206:         "enable_judge": bool(section.get("enable_judge", defaults.enable_judge)),
207:     }
208:     for key in _SCALARS:
209:         kwargs[key] = int(section.get(key, getattr(defaults, key)))
210:     _apply_legacy_timeout(section, kwargs)
211:     for key in _STRINGS:
212:         kwargs[key] = str(section.get(key) or getattr(defaults, key))
213:     for key in _OPTIONAL_STRINGS:
214:         value = section.get(key)
215:         kwargs[key] = str(value) if value else getattr(defaults, key)
216:     for key in _OPTIONAL_SLUGS:
217:         value = section.get(key)
218:         # A configured slug is folded on the way in so ``fb/lane`` and
219:         # ``fb_lane`` cannot produce two different test file names, and folded
220:         # through the naming rule so a long slug keeps the part of itself that
221:         # makes it a different lane.
222:         kwargs[key] = lane_slug_token(str(value)) if value else getattr(defaults, key)
223:     for key in _BOOLS:
224:         kwargs[key] = bool(section.get(key, getattr(defaults, key)))
225:     return GateConfig(**kwargs)

304:     """The result of running the gate's whole deterministic test set at one head.

307:     Verify needs that distinction and not just the count: a verifier's test that
308:     exits 0 is evidence the claim is *not* a blocker, however few ids it parsed.
309:     """

327: class GateTestRunner:
328:     """Runs the gate's test set at a worktree, memory-capped and slot-bounded.
329: 
330:     Two constraints are enforced here rather than trusted to the agents: every
331:     pytest is memory-capped (a 36GB runaway is a real failure mode on this
332:     machine), and every pytest holds a slot from the smaller test pool, so a
333:     wide verifier fan-out cannot launch twenty memory-capped processes at once.
334:     """

336:     def __init__(
337:         self,
338:         *,
339:         root: Path,
340:         memory: str = "6G",
341:         timeout_s: int = 900,
342:         package_dir: str | None = None,
343:         pool: SlotPool | None = None,
344:         use_systemd: bool | None = None,
345:     ) -> None:
346:         self.root = root
347:         self.memory = memory
348:         self.timeout_s = timeout_s
349:         self.package_dir = package_dir
350:         self.pool = pool
351:         self.use_systemd = systemd_run_available() if use_systemd is None else use_systemd
352:

354:         return find_test_packages(self.root, test_files, package_dir=self.package_dir)
355: 
356:     def pytest_hint(self, test_file: str) -> str:
357:         """The exact memory-capped command the agents are told to run."""
358:         package = self.packages_for([test_file])
359:         rel_dir = package[0].rel_dir if package else "."
360:         cmd = build_pytest_command(
361:             [to_package_path(rel_dir, test_file)],
362:             memory=self.memory,
363:             use_systemd=self.use_systemd,
364:             package_dir=self.root / rel_dir,
365:         )
366:         return f"(cd {self.root / rel_dir} && {' '.join(cmd)})"
367: 
368:     def test_dir_hint(self, test_file: str) -> str:
369:         package = self.packages_for([test_file])
370:         rel_dir = package[0].rel_dir if package else "."
371:         return f"{rel_dir}/tests" if rel_dir != "." else "tests"

373:     def run(self, test_files: list[str]) -> TestRun:
374:         """Run *test_files* grouped per owning package; collect failing node ids."""
375:         if not test_files:

407: class GateTestArchive:
408:     """Keeps gate-written test files so a fixer push cannot drop them.
409: 
410:     The gate tests live only in the worktree it created; the fixer pushes
411:     product code to the PR branch, so those test files would disappear at the
412:     next round. The archive copies each one out and materialises it back into
413:     every subsequent worktree at its original repo-relative path.
414:     """
415: 
416:     def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:
417:         self.dir = root / "tests"
418:         self.dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
419: 
420:     def stored_tests(self) -> list[Path]:
421:         """Every gate-written test the archive still holds, in name order.
422: 
423:         The archive is the only place a verifier's test survives a fixer push,
424:         so a later run that wants the gate's own evidence has to be able to ask
425:         what is in here. A fresh pipeline's ``evidence.gate_tests`` is always
426:         empty — it only records what *this* run produced — so a recheck driven
427:         by a new process could never see the archived tests.
428:         """
429:         return sorted(p for p in self.dir.glob("test_gate_*.py") if p.is_file())
430: 
431:     def store(self, source: Path) -> Path | None:
432:         if not source.is_file():
433:             return None
434:         target = self.dir / source.name
435:         shutil.copy2(source, target)
436:         return target
437: 
438:     def materialise(self, worktree: Path, rel_paths: list[str]) -> list[str]:
439:         """Copy archived tests back into *worktree*; return those restored."""
440:         restored: list[str] = []
441:         for rel in rel_paths:
442:             dest = worktree / rel
443:             if dest.is_file():
444:                 continue
445:             archived = self.dir / Path(rel).name
446:             if not archived.is_file():
447:                 continue
448:             dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
449:             shutil.copy2(archived, dest)
450:             restored.append(rel)
451:         return restored

"""Shared pytest fixtures for agent_fleet tests."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import pytest

from agent_fleet.config import load_fleet_config
from agent_fleet.hooks import FleetTask
from agent_fleet.personas import YamlPersonaResolver
from agent_fleet.runner import TaskRunner

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Callable

    from agent_fleet.hooks import LLMBackend

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


@pytest.fixture
def fleet_config_with_session_backend(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> Callable[[LLMBackend], TaskRunner]:
    """Return a factory that builds a TaskRunner wired with the given backend.

    The runner is pre-configured with a single FleetTask (persona="coder",
    pipeline="simple") and uses tmp_path as the workspace so tests can call
    runner.run(task_id=..., pipeline=...) without real filesystem setup.
    """
    fleet_config = load_fleet_config(ROOT / "fleet.example.yaml")
    resolver = YamlPersonaResolver(fleet_config)
    task = FleetTask(
        goal="Test task",
        context="",
        persona="coder",
        workspace=str(tmp_path),
        pipeline="simple",
    )

    def _make_runner(backend: LLMBackend) -> TaskRunner:
        return TaskRunner(
            backend=backend,
            fleet_config=fleet_config,
            persona_resolver=resolver,
            task=task,
            workspace=tmp_path,
        )

    return _make_runner
---YAML gate section---
gate:
  # Backend + model for the find / verify / fix roles (must satisfy model_policy).
  backend: cmd
  model: stealth/space-bunny-alpha

  # The judge runs on its own backend/model. The gate spends at most one judge
  # call for the main ruling and at most one recheck call, and only for
  # untestable claims.
  judge_backend: grok
  judge_model: step-5-preview

  # Parallel lens reviewers, each with ONE focus. Report blockers only; an
  # empty findings list is a normal, good outcome. Replace the mapping to
  # change the lens set, or use a list to keep the default focus text:
  #   lenses: [correctness, contract, prodsafety, spec]
  lenses:
    correctness: >-
      Logic errors, wrong results, broken edge cases, error handling,
      concurrency/race bugs, regressions of existing behaviour.
    contract: >-
      Public API/MCP/schema contract breaks, response shape, params,
      docs/OpenAPI drift vs behaviour, backwards compatibility, missing
      tests for promised behaviour.
    prodsafety: >-
      Production data safety and ops: data loss, destructive writes,
      unbounded memory/CPU on the VPS, missing locks/atomicity, unsafe
      migrations, performance regressions on hot paths, secrets exposure.
    spec: >-
      Conformance to the task specification supplied with --task-file:
      required items missing or implemented differently from what was asked.

  # Cap on candidate claims carried into verify, and on parallel reviewers.
  max_candidates: 12
  max_parallel_lenses: 8
  max_parallel_verifiers: 6

  # Fix rounds continue while the failing set strictly shrinks and no new
  # failures appear. max_fix_rounds is only a safety net against a run that
  # keeps making one-test-at-a-time progress — the stopping rule is
  # convergence, not the round count.
  max_fix_rounds: 4
  enable_fix: true
  enable_judge: true

  # Base branch for the diff the reviewers read; push_branch defaults to the
  # PR's own head branch.
  base_branch: main

  # Per-stage agent budgets (seconds), and the deterministic test budget. The
  # stages are split because they do different work: a fixer has to commit,
  # push and wait on a test suite, which never fits in a reviewer's budget.
  # A stage that runs out of budget is a dead agent and fails closed — the run
  # escalates rather than reading the silence as "no findings".
  lens_timeout_s: 2400
  verify_timeout_s: 2400
  judge_timeout_s: 2400
  fix_timeout_s: 5400
  test_timeout_s: 900

  # Every pytest the gate launches is memory-capped: a runaway suite once
  # consumed 36GB. The cap is used as given; the gate never raises it.
  test_memory: 6G

  # Machine-wide admission: these size the shared cross-process slot pools
  # under ~/.agent-fleet/slots, so several independent fleet processes on this
  # box share one budget instead of each getting its own. The test pool is
  # deliberately much smaller than the agent pool — pytest, not the agent, is
  # what exhausts memory.
  agent_slots: 24
  test_slots: 4

  # Force every test into one package directory when the repo's root
  # pyproject.toml is not the one that owns the tests. Leave unset for the
  # normal case, where the gate resolves each test's owning package.
  # package_dir: api

def run_pytest(
    package_dir: Path,
    test_files: Sequence[str],
    *,
    memory: str = "6G",
    timeout_s: int = 900,
    use_systemd: bool | None = None,
    cache_dir: Path | None = None,
    cache_ttl_s: int = DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL_S,
    prune_ttl_s: int = DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL_S,
) -> PytestResult:
    """Run the given tests from *package_dir* under a memory cap.

    Never raises on a non-zero exit — the caller inspects
    :attr:`PytestResult.infra_error` to tell "the code is broken" apart from
    "pytest could not run".

    With *cache_dir* set, a run whose worktree tree hash and test list match a
    stored result is served from disk instead of re-running pytest. A worktree
    that is not a git repo (or a git that cannot write a tree) simply runs
    uncached rather than failing.
    """
    if not test_files:
        return PytestResult(returncode=PYTEST_OK, stdout="", stderr="")
    key = None
    cache_root = cache_dir.expanduser() if cache_dir is not None else None
    if cache_root is not None:
        prune_cache(cache_root, prune_ttl_s)
        tree = worktree_tree_hash(package_dir)
        if tree is not None:
            key = cache_key(tree, test_files, package=str(package_dir))
            cached = cache_load(cache_root, key, ttl_s=cache_ttl_s)
            if cached is not None:
                logger.info("gate pytest: cache hit %s (%d file(s))", key[:12], len(test_files))
                return cached
    cmd = build_pytest_command(
        test_files, memory=memory, use_systemd=use_systemd, package_dir=package_dir
    )
    logger.debug("gate pytest: %s (cwd=%s)", " ".join(cmd), package_dir)
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            cwd=package_dir,
            timeout=timeout_s,
            check=False,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        # A timeout is an infra failure, not evidence the code is broken.
        return PytestResult(
            returncode=PYTEST_INFRA_ERROR,
            stdout="",
            stderr=f"pytest timed out after {timeout_s}s",
        )
    except OSError as exc:
        return PytestResult(returncode=PYTEST_INFRA_ERROR, stdout="", stderr=str(exc))
    result = PytestResult(
        returncode=completed.returncode,
        stdout=completed.stdout or "",
        stderr=completed.stderr or "",
    )
    if key is not None and cache_root is not None:
        cache_store(cache_root, key, result)
    return result

    :attr:`PytestResult.infra_error` to tell "the code is broken" apart from
    "pytest could not run".

    stored result is served from disk instead of re-running pytest. A worktree
    that is not a git repo (or a git that cannot write a tree) simply runs
    uncached rather than failing.

        tree = worktree_tree_hash(package_dir)

def verify(self, worktree: Path, findings: list[Finding], *, source: str) -> None:
        """Verify each testable claim with one failing test, run by the pipeline.

        The verifiers run in parallel, but their tests are re-run in ONE pytest
        invocation: a claim's verdict is only believable if its own test fails,
        and N sequential memory-capped pytest processes is the slowest part of a
        gate run. The batched run is fallible in exactly one way that matters —
        a collection or infra error (rc >= 2) poisons every claim at once — so
        that case falls back to re-running each file on its own, keeping the
        per-claim bar identical to the unbatched one.
        """
        for finding in findings:
            if not finding.testable:
                # Never drop a claim the lens could not frame as a test: the judge rules on it.
                self.evidence.untestable.append(finding.to_dict())
                self._log("gate.verify.untestable", finding=finding.id, reason="lens-marked")
        testable = [f for f in findings if f.testable]
        if not testable:
            return
        model = self._model_for(
            backend_name=self.config.backend, model=self.config.model, role=ROLE_VERIFIER
        )
        runner = self._runner_for(worktree)

        def _one(finding: Finding) -> _PendingVerify | None:
            return self._ask_verifier(
                finding, worktree=worktree, runner=runner, model=model, source=source
            )

        workers = max(1, self.config.max_parallel_verifiers)
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
            pending = [p for p in pool.map(_one, testable) if p is not None]

        self._rerun_verifications(pending, worktree=worktree, runner=runner, source=source)

    @dataclass
    class _PendingVerify:
        """A CONFIRMED verdict whose test still has to be re-run by the pipeline.

        Carrying the worktree path alongside the report is what lets the batched
        re-run build its file list: by the time the phase completes, every
        verifier has written its test, so the set is known.
        """

        finding: Finding
        report: Any  # noqa: ANN401 - VerifyReport
        rel: str
        test_path: Path

    def _ask_verifier(
        self,
        finding: Finding,
        *,
        worktree: Path,
        runner: GateTestRunner,
        model: str,
        source: str,
    ) -> _PendingVerify | None:
        """Run the verifier for one claim; return its pending re-run, or ``None``.

        Everything decided here is decided without touching pytest: an invalid
        answer, a REJECTED/UNTESTABLE verdict, or a test file that was never
        written all reject the claim outright. Only a CONFIRMED verdict that
        names a file that exists survives to :meth:`_rerun_verifications`.
        """
        test_name = gate_test_name(self.lane_slug, finding.id)
        prompt = verify_prompt(
            finding=finding,
            worktree=str(worktree),
            base_branch=resolve_diff_base(worktree, self.config.base_branch),
            head_sha=(self._head_sha(worktree) or "")[:9],
            pr_number=self.pr_number,
            test_dir_hint=runner.test_dir_hint(finding.file or "x"),
            pytest_cmd_hint=runner.pytest_hint(test_name),
            test_file_name=test_name,
        )
        answer = self._call_required(
            role="verify",
            subject=finding.id,
            invalid_ok=True,
            lens=finding.lens,
            backend=self.backend,
            prompt=prompt,
            model=model,
            cwd=worktree,
            timeout_s=self.config.stage_timeout(ROLE_VERIFIER),
            validate=validate_verify,
        )
        if answer is None:
            self.evidence.reject(finding, "verifier answer invalid (no proof)")
            return None
        report = VerifyReport.from_dict(answer.data)
        if report.verdict is VerifyVerdict.UNTESTABLE:
            self.evidence.untestable.append(finding.to_dict())
            self._log("gate.verify.untestable", finding=finding.id)
            return None
        if report.verdict is not VerifyVerdict.CONFIRMED or not report.test_file:
            self.evidence.reject(finding, f"verifier: {report.verdict.value}: {report.reason}")
            self._log("gate.verify.rejected", finding=finding.id, reason=report.reason[:160])
            return None
        rel = _normalise_repo_path(report.test_file)
        test_path = worktree / rel
        if not test_path.is_file():
            self.evidence.reject(finding, "verifier named a test file that does not exist")
            self._log("gate.verify.discarded", finding=finding.id, reason="no test file")
            return None
        return GatePipeline._PendingVerify(
            finding=finding, report=report, rel=rel, test_path=test_path
        )

    def _rerun_verifications(
        self,
        pending: list[_PendingVerify],
        *,
        worktree: Path,
        runner: GateTestRunner,
        source: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Re-run every CONFIRMED claim's test, batching them into one invocation.

        The bar is unchanged: a claim is confirmed only when a test in its OWN
        file fails on an assertion. Batching only changes how many processes pay
        for it, and it can only ever be a *weakening* if the run is not usable
        (rc >= 2, a collection error that reports nothing per file), which is
        why that case drops back to one invocation per file.
        """
        if not pending:
            return
        files = sorted({p.rel for p in pending})
        run = runner.run(files)
        self._log(
            "gate.verify.batched_rerun",
            files=len(files),
            failing=run.count,
            infra_error=bool(run.infra_error),
        )
        if run.infra_error:
            # The batched run told us nothing about any individual file, so it
            # cannot confirm anything. Re-run each on its own — the same
            # fail-closed bar, just without the batching.
            self._log(
                "gate.verify.batched_rerun_fallback",
                reason=run.infra_error[:160],
                files=len(files),
            )
            for item in pending:
                single = runner.run([item.rel])
                self._settle(item, single, source=source)
            return
        for item in pending:
            self._settle(item, run, source=source)

    def _settle(self, item: _PendingVerify, run: TestRun, *, source: str) -> None:
        """Confirm or discard one claim against *run*, and record which.

        When the run was batched, only this claim's own failing tests count.
        When it was a single-file run, the run is that file's whole result, so a
        plain ``tests_failed`` is the same test as a per-file attribution.
        """
        own = run.failed_tests_in(item.rel)
        batched = bool(own) or not run.failed_tests_in.__self__.failing or True
        del batched  # per-file attribution is correct for both run shapes
        if run.infra_error:
            self.evidence.reject(item.finding, f"verifier test could not run: {run.infra_error}")
            self._log(
                "gate.verify.discarded", finding=item.finding.id, reason=run.infra_error[:160]
            )
            _unlink(item.test_path)
            return
        if not own:
            # The verifier claimed CONFIRMED but its test does not fail on a test
            # assertion. The pipeline believes the test, not the verdict.
            reason = f"verifier test did not fail (failing={run.count})"
            self.evidence.reject(item.finding, reason)
            self._log("gate.verify.discarded", finding=item.finding.id, reason=reason)
            _unlink(item.test_path)
            return
        self.archive.store(item.test_path)
        self.evidence.confirmed.append(
            {
                **item.finding.to_dict(),
                "source": source,
                "test_file": item.rel,
                "reason": item.report.reason,
            }
        )
        self.evidence.gate_tests.append(item.rel)
        self._log("gate.verify.confirmed", finding=item.finding.id, test_file=item.rel)

"""Tests for the gate's pytest result cache.

The cache exists because a gate run executes the same test set many times — once
per verified claim, then every fix round. The safety property is the whole point:
a result is replayed ONLY when the worktree is byte-for-byte the same tree the
run saw, uncommitted edits and untracked files included. Every test here is
written to fail if that weakens into "reuse the last result".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from agent_fleet.gate import pytest_runner as pr
from agent_fleet.gate.pytest_runner import (
    DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR,
    PytestResult,
    cache_key,
    cache_load,
    cache_store,
    prune_cache,
    worktree_tree_hash,
)


def _git(*args: str, cwd: Path) -> str:
    completed = subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    )
    return completed.stdout.strip()


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """A committed git repo with a package layout the runner understands."""
    root = tmp_path / "repo"
    (root / "tests").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        '[build-system]\nrequires=["setuptools"]\nbuild-backend="setuptools.build_meta"\n'
        '[project]\nname="cache-fixture"\nversion="0.0.0"\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (root / "code.py").write_text("VALUE = 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "tests" / "test_a.py").write_text("def test_a():\n    assert True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    _git("init", "-q", cwd=root)
    _git("config", "user.email", "gate@local", cwd=root)
    _git("config", "user.name", "gate", cwd=root)
    _git("add", "-A", cwd=root)
    _git("commit", "-qm", "init", cwd=root)
    return root


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# worktree_tree_hash — the key must cover the WHOLE worktree
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_tree_hash_is_stable_when_nothing_changes(repo: Path) -> None:
    assert worktree_tree_hash(repo) == worktree_tree_hash(repo)


def test_tree_hash_tracks_a_committed_change(repo: Path) -> None:
    before = worktree_tree_hash(repo)
    (repo / "code.py").write_text("VALUE = 2\n", encoding="utf-8")
    _git("add", "-A", cwd=repo)
    _git("commit", "-qm", "change", cwd=repo)
    assert worktree_tree_hash(repo) != before


def test_tree_hash_tracks_an_uncommitted_edit(repo: Path) -> None:
    """A dirty worktree is the normal state here: the fixer edits without committing."""
    before = worktree_tree_hash(repo)
    (repo / "code.py").write_text("VALUE = 99\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert worktree_tree_hash(repo) != before


def test_tree_hash_tracks_an_untracked_file(repo: Path) -> None:
    """A verifier's brand-new test is untracked; ignoring it would replay a stale verdict."""
    before = worktree_tree_hash(repo)
    (repo / "tests" / "test_gate_new.py").write_text("x = 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert worktree_tree_hash(repo) != before


def test_tree_hash_tracks_a_deletion(repo: Path) -> None:
    before = worktree_tree_hash(repo)
    (repo / "code.py").unlink()
    assert worktree_tree_hash(repo) != before


def test_tree_hash_does_not_disturb_the_real_index(repo: Path) -> None:
    """The gate shares this worktree with running agents; the index must survive."""
    (repo / "code.py").write_text("VALUE = 3\n", encoding="utf-8")
    before = _git("diff", "--cached", "--name-only", cwd=repo)
    worktree_tree_hash(repo)
    assert _git("diff", "--cached", "--name-only", cwd=repo) == before


def test_tree_hash_is_none_outside_a_git_repo(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """A non-repo must degrade to "run uncached", never raise or return a bogus key."""
    plain = tmp_path / "plain"
    plain.mkdir()
    assert worktree_tree_hash(plain) is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# cache_key
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_cache_key_ignores_test_order() -> None:
    a = cache_key("tree", ["t2.py", "t1.py"], package=".")
    b = cache_key("tree", ["t1.py", "t2.py"], package=".")
    assert a == b


def test_cache_key_changes_with_the_test_list() -> None:
    assert cache_key("tree", ["t1.py"], package=".") != cache_key("tree", ["t1.py", "t2.py"], package=".")


def test_cache_key_changes_with_the_tree() -> None:
    assert cache_key("t1", ["t1.py"], package=".") != cache_key("t2", ["t1.py"], package=".")


def test_cache_key_changes_with_the_package() -> None:
    """The same relative path is a different file under a different package root."""
    assert cache_key("t", ["tests/test_a.py"], package=".") != cache_key(
        "t", ["tests/test_a.py"], package="api"
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# store / load
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_round_trip_preserves_result(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    result = PytestResult(returncode=1, stdout="FAILED a::t\n1 failed", stderr="warn")
    assert cache_store(cache, "k", result)
    assert cache_load(cache, "k", ttl_s=3600) == result


def test_miss_when_absent(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    assert cache_load(tmp_path / "nope", "k", ttl_s=3600) is None


def test_only_real_results_are_cached(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """rc >= 2 is a collection/infra failure; replaying it would fake a verdict."""
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    for rc in (2, 3, 4, 5):
        assert not cache_store(cache, f"k{rc}", PytestResult(returncode=rc, stdout="boom"))
    for rc in (0, 1):
        assert cache_store(cache, f"k{rc}", PytestResult(returncode=rc, stdout="ok"))
    assert cache_load(cache, "k2", ttl_s=3600) is None


def test_expired_entry_is_a_miss_and_not_returned(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    cache_store(cache, "k", PytestResult(returncode=0, stdout="ok"))
    old = 10_000.0
    import os

    os.utime(cache / "k.json", (old, old))
    assert cache_load(cache, "k", ttl_s=3600, now=old + 3601) is None


def test_entry_within_ttl_is_returned(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    cache_store(cache, "k", PytestResult(returncode=0, stdout="ok"))
    assert cache_load(cache, "k", ttl_s=3600) is not None


def test_corrupt_entry_is_a_miss_not_a_crash(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    cache.mkdir()
    (cache / "k.json").write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
    assert cache_load(cache, "k", ttl_s=3600) is None


def test_entry_from_another_format_version_is_dropped(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    cache.mkdir()
    (cache / "k.json").write_text('{"v": 999, "rc": 0, "stdout": "old"}', encoding="utf-8")
    assert cache_load(cache, "k", ttl_s=3600) is None


def test_prune_removes_only_expired_entries(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    cache_store(cache, "fresh", PytestResult(returncode=0, stdout="ok"))
    cache_store(cache, "stale", PytestResult(returncode=0, stdout="ok"))
    import os

    os.utime(cache / "stale.json", (0, 0))
    now = 200_000.0
    assert prune_cache(cache, 3600, now=now) == 1
    assert cache_load(cache, "fresh", ttl_s=3600, now=now) is not None
    assert cache_load(cache, "stale", ttl_s=3600, now=now) is None


def test_prune_on_a_missing_dir_is_a_noop(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    assert prune_cache(tmp_path / "absent", 3600) == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# run_pytest integration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_run_pytest_serves_a_repeat_run_from_cache(
    repo: Path, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    calls: list[list[str]] = []

    def fake_run(cmd: list[str], **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        calls.append(cmd)
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 1, "FAILED tests/test_a.py::test_a\n1 failed", "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    first = pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=cache)
    second = pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=cache)

    assert len(calls) == 1, "second identical run should not have launched pytest"
    assert second.returncode == first.returncode == 1
    assert second.stdout == first.stdout


def test_any_file_change_misses_the_cache(
    repo: Path, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """The regression this cache could plausibly ship: a stale hit after an edit."""
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    calls: list[list[str]] = []

    def fake_run(cmd: list[str], **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        calls.append(cmd)
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, "1 passed", "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=cache)
    (repo / "code.py").write_text("VALUE = 42\n", encoding="utf-8")
    pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=cache)

    assert len(calls) == 2, "an uncommitted edit must invalidate the cached result"


def test_unchanged_worktree_hits_cache_across_a_different_test_list(
    repo: Path, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    calls: list[list[str]] = []

    def fake_run(cmd: list[str], **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        calls.append(cmd)
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, "1 passed", "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    (repo / "tests" / "test_b.py").write_text("def test_b():\n    assert True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=cache)
    pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py", "tests/test_b.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=cache)
    pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=cache)

    assert len(calls) == 2, "only the new test list should have been run"


def test_infra_error_is_not_replayed(
    repo: Path, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    cache = tmp_path / "cache"
    rcs = iter([2, 0])

    def fake_run(cmd: list[str], **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, next(rcs), "collection error", "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    first = pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=cache)
    second = pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=cache)

    assert first.returncode == 2
    assert second.returncode == 0, "a cached infra error must be re-run, not replayed"


def test_no_cache_dir_means_no_caching(
    repo: Path, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    calls: list[list[str]] = []

    def fake_run(cmd: list[str], **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        calls.append(cmd)
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, "1 passed", "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False)
    pr.run_pytest(repo, ["tests/test_a.py"], use_systemd=False)
    assert len(calls) == 2


def test_empty_test_list_never_touches_the_cache(
    repo: Path, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    def boom(*a: object, **k: object) -> None:
        raise AssertionError("no subprocess should be launched")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", boom)
    assert pr.run_pytest(repo, [], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=tmp_path / "c").passed


def test_non_git_worktree_still_runs_uncached(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """A tree hash is unobtainable without git, and that must not break the run."""
    plain = tmp_path / "plain"
    plain.mkdir()
    calls: list[list[str]] = []

    def fake_run(cmd: list[str], **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        calls.append(cmd)
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, "1 passed", "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    assert pr.run_pytest(plain, ["t.py"], use_systemd=False, cache_dir=tmp_path / "c").passed
    assert len(calls) == 1


def test_default_cache_dir_is_under_agent_fleet() -> None:
    assert DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR == Path("~/.agent-fleet/cache/gate-tests")

"""Tests for the gate's pytest result cache.

The cache exists because a gate run executes the same test set many times — once
per verified claim, then every fix round. The safety property is the whole point:
a result is replayed ONLY when the worktree is byte-for-byte the same tree the
run saw, uncommitted edits and untracked files included. Every test here is

def _git(*args: str, cwd: Path) -> str:
    completed = subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    )
    return completed.stdout.strip()


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """A committed git repo with a package layout the runner understands."""
    root = tmp_path / "repo"
    (root / "tests").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        '[build-system]\nrequires=["setuptools"]\nbuild-backend="setuptools.build_meta"\n'
        '[project]\nname="cache-fixture"\nversion="0.0.0"\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (root / "code.py").write_text("VALUE = 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "tests" / "test_a.py").write_text("def test_a():\n    assert True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    _git("init", "-q", cwd=root)
